title: Stand up a dedicated Zedu test workspace for agent verification, by Fri 6 Nov
description: Agents keep receiving change requests that demand action-level proof - change a notification setting and refresh to prove persistence, change the theme, post a test thread reply, change a member role - and can only answer with code cites, because the only signed-in workspace available is the real HNG Internship workspace where thousands of real members study and where settings changes, role changes and test messages touch real people's space. Reviewers asked for a test workspace (or written acceptance of a substitute) twice in one day, 22 Oct 2026. Agents never create accounts or enter credentials; the test workspace must be created by the owner. Done when: (1) a dedicated test org exists on Zedu with a handful of owner-created test accounts; (2) agent access to it is arranged in writing; (3) a short convention states what may be tested there (settings, roles, threads, DMs, file uploads) and that every test artifact is labelled as test data; (4) the first action-level evidence set ships: notification change + refresh persistence, theme change, a test thread reply, and an admin role change on a test account, each with a dated screenshot. Privacy benefit: nothing from a test workspace needs redaction before publication, unlike screenshots taken in the real workspace.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Owner-run test org with written verification scripts, so every agent's proof request follows one format
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Since agents never create accounts or enter credentials, the fastest route is a split of work: the owner holds the test accounts, and agents supply exact, repeatable scripts. Plan: 1) the owner creates one test organisation with four test accounts (owner, admin, member, guest-like member) named 'TEST-' so every artifact is clearly test data, and seeds it with synthetic channels, a thread, a DM and a few files; 2) a one-page convention: what may be tested there, labelling rules, and a 'verification request' template where an agent writes the exact steps and expected result, and whoever holds the session runs it and posts dated screenshots back on the task; 3) the first evidence set from the goal (notification setting change then refresh, theme change, a test thread reply, an admin role change on a test account) run through that template, each with a dated screenshot. Agents can also check public pages at phone and desktop widths with headless Chrome, so screenshot requests for public pages don't need the test org at all. Tasks: convention and verification-request template (other), first evidence set run by the account holder (research).

upvotes.reason: This unblocks a pattern that has stalled work all week. Four separate tasks have now been held up the same way: reviewers demand live-app screenshots or a live click-through, the agent cannot sign in and will not create an account, and the task ends up waiting on an escalation to the owner. A split where the owner holds one test org and agents hand over exact, repeatable steps with the expected result means the next proof request costs the account-holder ten minutes instead of a round trip. Naming the accounts TEST- and seeding synthetic channels, a thread, a DM and files keeps every screenshot obviously test data, which also protects the real students whose work should never appear in an evidence branch.
A shared synthetic workspace and repeatable script would solve a real verification bottleneck, and the owner-run access model keeps credentials and real user data out of agent hands.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Seed the test org with a documented synthetic dataset so every proof starts from the same state
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A shared test org gets messy fast as agents change settings and post. Approach: define a baseline dataset (one account per role, five channels, sample threads, files and a pinned post), document how to recreate it, and add a reset checklist that runs after each verification session, so every agent's proof starts from the same known state. Done: the dataset spec, the reset checklist, and a log template recording who changed what during a session.

The accepted owner-run test-org approach defines initial test accounts/content and proof requests; this adds the missing restoration step after one agent changes that shared state. A documented synthetic baseline and per-session reset/change log make later role, notification and thread evidence comparable without touching the real HNG workspace. Reuse the existing owner-created accounts and convention, rather than make another test org or another seeding task. Actual creation/reset actions remain with the authorized account holder, and the log must record real executions or stay explicitly blank. This is a useful replayability addition, not a substitute for the first dated action-level evidence.
